title: Why big animals have deep voices
group: HOWN — How and Why in Nature
examples: Why do big animals make low sounds?
Why do men usually have deeper voices?
Why does a mouse squeak but a lion roar?

explain.say: A mouse squeaks and an elephant rumbles. The pitch of a voice depends mostly on the size of the parts that vibrate.

draw.text: Why big animals have deep voices

explain.say: Mammals make sound with vocal folds in the throat, which vibrate as air rushes past. Small, light folds vibrate very fast and make high-pitched sounds.
Longer, heavier folds vibrate more slowly, so they make lower sounds, just as a long, thick guitar string sounds deeper than a short, thin one.
Bigger animals have bigger vocal folds and bigger throats, so their voices are deeper. In people, voices drop at puberty as the vocal folds grow longer and thicker, especially in boys.

faq.q: Why do big animals make low sounds?
faq.a: Big animals have long, heavy vocal folds that vibrate slowly, and slow vibrations make low pitches. Their large throats and chests also boost deep sounds.

faq.q: Why does a mouse squeak but a lion roar?
faq.a: A mouse's tiny vocal folds vibrate thousands of times a second, giving a high squeak. A lion's big, thick vocal folds vibrate slowly, giving a deep roar.
asks: How do lions roar so deep?

faq.q: Why do men usually have deeper voices?
faq.a: During puberty, the vocal folds of boys grow longer and thicker than girls', so they vibrate more slowly. Adult men often speak at around 120 vibrations a second, women at around 200.
Vocal folds, sometimes called vocal cords, are two bands of muscle and tissue in your voice box. Air from your lungs makes them vibrate, which produces your voice.

faq.q: Can an animal change its pitch?
faq.a: Yes. By tightening or relaxing the vocal folds, animals and people can raise or lower their pitch, like tuning a guitar string. Size sets the range they can reach.
asks: How do singers reach high notes?
How do we change our pitch?

facts: Longer, heavier vocal folds vibrate more slowly and produce lower-pitched sounds.
Adult men often speak at around 100 to 120 hertz and adult women at around 200 hertz.
